<skill_content name="test-driven-development">
# Skill: test-driven-development

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  # A PR with no description gives a reviewer nothing to check the diff
  # against, so an empty body fails the build before any expensive job runs.
  pr-body:
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Require a non-empty pull request body
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

"""The pull request template and the CI gate that requires a non-empty body."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
TEMPLATE = ROOT / ".github" / "pull_request_template.md"
WORKFLOW = ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "ci.yml"

REQUIRED_SECTIONS = ("## Summary", "## What changed", "## Verification", "## Related issue")


def test_the_template_asks_for_the_four_sections() -> None:
    template = TEMPLATE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    for section in REQUIRED_SECTIONS:
        assert section in template, f"{section} is missing from the PR template"


def test_ci_runs_the_body_gate_only_for_pull_requests() -> None:
    workflow = WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    assert "\n  pr-body:\n" in workflow
    assert "github.event_name == 'pull_request'" in workflow


def test_the_gate_reads_the_body_through_the_api_and_fails_when_empty() -> None:

    assert "gh pr view" in gate
    assert "--json body" in gate

"""Generate and publish end-user "Download & Run" instructions for a GitHub release.

Pure functions:
    build_instructions_section(tag, repo, artifacts, checksums_text) -> str
    apply_instructions(body, section) -> str

CLI (``main``): fetches the release body/assets via ``gh``, grabs
``checksums.txt`` via ``curl``, builds the instructions section, applies it
idempotently to the release body, and publishes with ``gh release edit``
(unless ``--dry-run``).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

DOWNLOAD_START = "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_START -->"
DOWNLOAD_END = "<!-- AGENTIC_ODI_DOWNLOAD_END -->"

GITHUB_RELEASES = "https://github.com"


def _archive_target(name: str) -> str:
    """Strip the ``odi_<version>_`` prefix and archive suffix to expose ``<os>_<arch>``."""
    stem = name
    for suffix in (".tar.gz", ".zip"):
        if stem.endswith(suffix):
            stem = stem[: -len(suffix)]
            break
    if stem.startswith("odi_"):
        stem = stem[len("odi_") :]
    parts = stem.split("_")
    if len(parts) >= 3:
        return "_".join(parts[1:])
    return stem


def _platform(target: str) -> str:
    mapping = {
        "linux_x86_64": "Linux (x86_64)",
        "linux_arm64": "Linux (ARM64)",
        "macos_x86_64": "macOS (Intel)",
        "macos_arm64": "macOS (Apple Silicon)",
        "windows_x86_64": "Windows (x86_64)",
    }
    return mapping.get(target, target.replace("_", " ").title())


def _hash_for(checksums_text: str, name: str) -> str | None:
    for line in checksums_text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        hash_, sep, fname = line.partition("  ")
        if not sep:
            hash_, sep, fname = line.partition(" ")
        fname = fname.lstrip("*").strip()
        if fname == name:
            return hash_.strip()
    return None


def build_instructions_section(
    tag: str, repo: str, artifacts: list[dict], checksums_text: str
) -> str:
    version = tag.lstrip("v")
    dl_base = f"{GITHUB_RELEASES}/{repo}/releases/download/{tag}"

    release_artifacts = [
        a for a in artifacts if a["name"] not in ("checksums.txt", "install.sh", "install.ps1")
    ]

    lines: list[str] = []
    lines.append("## 📦 Download & Run")

"""Unit tests for scripts/pr_guards.py (issue #86)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

    GuardConfig,
    build_diff_args,
    changed_files_from_status,
    check_deletions,

    guard_diff_shape,

    parse_numstat,
)


def _release(path: str) -> str:
    return "v1.2.3"


# --- Gate 1: deletion budget -------------------------------------------------


def test_deleting_a_shipped_file_fails_and_names_the_release() -> None:
    errors = check_deletions(
        ["apps/old/thing.tsx"],
        allowlist=[],
        release_lookup=_release,
    )

    assert len(errors) == 1
    assert "apps/old/thing.tsx" in errors[0]
    assert "v1.2.3" in errors[0]


def test_an_empty_allowlist_denies_every_deletion() -> None:
    errors = check_deletions(
        ["a.py", "b.py"],
        allowlist=[],
        release_lookup=_release,
    )

    assert len(errors) == 2


def test_an_allowlisted_deletion_passes() -> None:
    allowlist = [{"path": "apps/old/thing.tsx", "issue": "123", "reason": "moved"}]

    errors = check_deletions(["apps/old/thing.tsx"], allowlist=allowlist, release_lookup=_release)

    assert errors == []


def test_the_allowlist_supports_globs() -> None:
    allowlist = [{"path": "apps/old/*.tsx", "issue": "123", "reason": "moved"}]

    errors = check_deletions(["apps/old/a.tsx", "apps/old/b.tsx"], allowlist, _release)

    assert errors == []


def test_missing_release_is_reported_as_unreleased() -> None:
    errors = check_deletions(["new.py"], allowlist=[], release_lookup=lambda _p: None)

    assert len(errors) == 1
    assert "unreleased" in errors[0]


# --- Gate 2: diff size -------------------------------------------------------


def test_exceeding_the_deletion_budget_fails() -> None:
    numstat = {"a.py": (0, 400), "b.py": (0, 200)}

    errors = check_diff_budget(numstat, GuardConfig(max_deletions=500))

    assert len(errors) == 1
    assert "600" in errors[0]


def test_staying_under_the_deletion_budget_passes() -> None:
    numstat = {"a.py": (10, 20)}

    assert check_diff_budget(numstat, GuardConfig(max_deletions=500)) == []


def test_generated_files_are_excluded_from_the_budget() -> None:
    numstat = {"uv.lock": (0, 5000), "package-lock.json": (0, 5000), "a.py": (1, 1)}

    assert check_diff_budget(numstat, GuardConfig(max_deletions=500)) == []


def test_generated_detection_covers_the_documented_paths() -> None:
    config = GuardConfig()

    for path in ("uv.lock", "apps/studio/src/api/schema.d.ts", "openapi.json", "coverage.xml"):
        assert is_generated(path, config), path
    assert not is_generated("apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/cli.py", config)


def test_exceeding_the_changed_file_budget_fails() -> None:
    numstat = {f"f{i}.py": (1, 0) for i in range(11)}

    errors = check_diff_budget(numstat, GuardConfig(max_changed_files=10))

    assert len(errors) == 1
    assert "11" in errors[0]


# --- Gate 3: branch freshness ------------------------------------------------


def test_a_stale_branch_is_a_warning_not_an_error() -> None:
    result = guard_diff_shape(
        deleted=[],
        numstat={},
        allowlist=[],
        config=GuardConfig(max_behind=50),
        release_lookup=_release,
        behind=51,
    )

    assert result.errors == []
    assert any("51" in warning for warning in result.warnings)


def test_a_fresh_branch_has_no_freshness_warning() -> None:
    result = guard_diff_shape(
        deleted=[],
        numstat={},
        allowlist=[],
        config=GuardConfig(max_behind=50),
        release_lookup=_release,
        behind=3,
    )

    assert result.warnings == []


def test_check_freshness_returns_the_warning() -> None:
    warnings = check_freshness(10, GuardConfig(max_behind=5))

    assert len(warnings) == 1


# --- Diff parsing and cumulative (three-dot) semantics ----------------------


def test_parse_name_status_handles_adds_modifies_and_deletes() -> None:
    status = "A\tnew.py\nM\told.py\nD\tgone.py\n"

    parsed = parse_name_status(status)

    assert parsed == [("A", "new.py", None), ("M", "old.py", None), ("D", "gone.py", None)]


def test_parse_name_status_handles_renames() -> None:
    parsed = parse_name_status("R100\told.py\tnew.py\n")

    assert parsed == [("R100", "new.py", "old.py")]


def test_parse_numstat_handles_binary_files() -> None:
    parsed = parse_numstat("10\t2\ta.py\n-\t-\tb.png\n")

    assert parsed == {"a.py": (10, 2), "b.png": (0, 0)}


def test_changed_files_from_status_counts_every_entry() -> None:
    parsed = parse_name_status("A\ta.py\nM\tb.py\nD\tc.py\n")

    assert changed_files_from_status(parsed) == 3


def test_diff_args_use_the_cumulative_three_dot_merge_base_diff() -> None:
    args = build_diff_args("origin/main", "HEAD")

    assert args == ["git", "diff", "--name-status", "origin/main...HEAD"]


def test_cumulative_diff_catches_a_mid_branch_tree_replacement(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    repo.mkdir()

    def git(*args: str) -> None:
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", *args],
            cwd=repo,
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )

    git("init", "-q", "-b", "main")
    git("config", "user.email", "test@example.com")
    git("config", "user.name", "Test")
    (repo / "shipped.py").write_text("shipped = True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    git("add", ".")
    git("commit", "-q", "-m", "base")

    git("checkout", "-q", "-b", "feature")
    (repo / "feature.py").write_text("feature = True\n", encoding="utf-8")
    git("add", ".")
    git("commit", "-q", "-m", "real work")

    (repo / "shipped.py").unlink()
    (repo / "feature.py").write_text("feature = False\n", encoding="utf-8")
    git("add", "-A")
    git("commit", "-q", "-m", "tree replacement")

    output = subprocess.run(
        build_diff_args("main", "HEAD"),
        cwd=repo,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    ).stdout

    deleted = [new for status, new, _old in parse_name_status(output) if status == "D"]

    assert deleted == ["shipped.py"]

"""Deterministic pull-request guardrails (issue #86).

The logic lives here, not in YAML, so every rule is unit-tested. The GitHub
workflow in ``.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml`` only gathers the diff and
calls this module.

Three deterministic gates (failures):
  * deletion budget - a PR may not delete a shipped file unless allowlisted
  * diff size       - a PR may not delete more than ``max_deletions`` lines
  * JSON block      - the machine-readable diff summary must match the diff

Two advisory gates (warnings):
  * body truth      - natural-language claims about files and tests
  * fabrication     - patterns that have shipped fabricated work before
  * branch freshness - a stale base is worth a rebase, not a block

Everything is computed on the cumulative ``base...HEAD`` diff, never per
commit. A tree-replacement commit buried in the middle of a branch stays
visible in the cumulative diff.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Mapping, Sequence

# Files that are regenerated by design. Their churn is not a signal.
DEFAULT_GENERATED_EXCLUSIONS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "uv.lock",
    "**/uv.lock",
    "package-lock.json",
    "**/package-lock.json",
    "yarn.lock",
    "**/yarn.lock",
    "pnpm-lock.yaml",
    "**/pnpm-lock.yaml",
    "Cargo.lock",
    "**/Cargo.lock",
    "poetry.lock",
    "**/poetry.lock",
    "*.lock",
    "**/openapi.json",
    "**/schema.d.ts",
    "**/coverage.xml",
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GuardConfig:
    """Tunable thresholds, read from ``.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml``."""

    max_deletions: int = 500
    max_changed_files: int = 2000
    max_behind: int = 50
    tolerance: float = 0.20
    generated_exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_GENERATED_EXCLUSIONS


@dataclass
class GuardResult:
    """Errors fail the build; warnings annotate the PR."""

    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def failed(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.errors)


ReleaseLookup = Callable[[str], str | None]


def build_diff_args(base_ref: str, head_ref: str) -> list[str]:
    """The cumulative diff. Three dots = merge-base diff, not last-commit."""
    return ["git", "diff", "--name-status", f"{base_ref}...{head_ref}"]


def parse_name_status(output: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str | None]]:
    """Parse ``git diff --name-status`` into (status, path, old_path) tuples."""
    entries: list[tuple[str, str, str | None]] = []
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        parts = line.split("\t")
        status = parts[0]
        if status.startswith("R") or status.startswith("C"):
            entries.append((status, parts[2], parts[1]))
        else:
            entries.append((status, parts[1], None))
    return entries


def parse_numstat(output: str) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
    """Parse ``git diff --numstat``; binary files count as (0, 0)."""
    stats: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    for line in output.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        added, deleted, path = line.split("\t", 2)
        stats[path] = (0 if added == "-" else int(added), 0 if deleted == "-" else int(deleted))
    return stats


def changed_files_from_status(entries: Sequence[tuple[str, str, str | None]]) -> int:
    return len(entries)


def is_generated(path: str, config: GuardConfig) -> bool:
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pattern) for pattern in config.generated_exclusions)


def _allowed(path: str, allowlist: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]]) -> bool:
    for entry in allowlist:
        pattern = str(entry.get("path", ""))
        if pattern and fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pattern):
            return True
    return False


def check_deletions(
    deleted: Sequence[str],
    allowlist: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
    release_lookup: ReleaseLookup,
) -> list[str]:
    """Fail every deletion that is not explicitly allowlisted."""
    errors: list[str] = []
    for path in deleted:
        if _allowed(path, allowlist):
            continue
        release = release_lookup(path)
        where = f"shipped in {release}" if release else "unreleased"
        errors.append(
            f"Deleted file {path!r} ({where}). Deleting a file that exists on the base "
            "branch is not allowed. If this is intentional, add an entry to "
            ".github/pr-guardrails/deletion-allowlist.yml naming the issue and reason."
        )
    return errors


def check_diff_budget(numstat: Mapping[str, tuple[int, int]], config: GuardConfig) -> list[str]:
    """Fail when the diff deletes too many lines or touches too many files."""
    counted = {path: stat for path, stat in numstat.items() if not is_generated(path, config)}
    deletions = sum(deleted for _added, deleted in counted.values())
    changed = len(counted)

    errors: list[str] = []
    if deletions > config.max_deletions:
        errors.append(
            f"The diff deletes {deletions} lines, over the {config.max_deletions}-line budget. "
            "Split the change, or add a generated-file exclusion for files that are "
            "regenerated by design."
        )
    if changed > config.max_changed_files:
        errors.append(
            f"The diff changes {changed} files, over the {config.max_changed_files}-file budget. "
            "Split the change."
        )
    return errors


def check_freshness(behind: int, config: GuardConfig) -> list[str]:
    """A stale base is a warning: rebases are best resolved by a human."""
    if behind > config.max_behind:
        return [
            f"This branch is {behind} commits behind the base branch "
            f"(limit {config.max_behind}). Rebase so the diff is computed against "
            "the current base."
        ]
    return []


def guard_diff_shape(
    *,
    deleted: Sequence[str],
    numstat: Mapping[str, tuple[int, int]],
    allowlist: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
    config: GuardConfig,
    release_lookup: ReleaseLookup,
    behind: int = 0,
) -> GuardResult:
    errors = check_deletions(deleted, allowlist, release_lookup)
    errors.extend(check_diff_budget(numstat, config))
    return GuardResult(errors=errors, warnings=check_freshness(behind, config))


def load_config(path: Path) -> GuardConfig:
    """Read ``config.yml``; a missing file keeps the defaults."""
    if not path.exists():
        return GuardConfig()
    import yaml

    raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    defaults = GuardConfig()
    return GuardConfig(
        max_deletions=int(raw.get("max_deletions", defaults.max_deletions)),
        max_changed_files=int(raw.get("max_changed_files", defaults.max_changed_files)),
        max_behind=int(raw.get("max_behind", defaults.max_behind)),
        tolerance=float(raw.get("tolerance", defaults.tolerance)),
        generated_exclusions=tuple(
            raw.get("generated_exclusions", defaults.generated_exclusions)
        ),
    )


def load_allowlist(path: Path) -> list[Mapping[str, object]]:
    """Read ``deletion-allowlist.yml``; a missing file denies every deletion."""
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    import yaml

    raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or []
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{path} must contain a list of deletion entries")
    return raw

# --- CLI ---------------------------------------------------------------------


def _git(*args: str) -> str:
    import subprocess

    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    ).stdout


def _release_lookup(base_ref: str) -> ReleaseLookup:
    cache: dict[str, str | None] = {}

    def lookup(path: str) -> str | None:
        if path in cache:
            return cache[path]
        release: str | None = None
        try:
            sha = _git("log", "-1", "--format=%H", base_ref, "--", path).strip()
            if sha:
                tags = _git("tag", "--contains", sha, "--sort=v:refname").splitlines()
                release = tags[0] if tags else None
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - an unknown release is "unreleased"
            release = None
        cache[path] = release
        return release

    return lookup


def _collect(base_ref: str) -> tuple[
    list[tuple[str, str, str | None]], dict[str, tuple[int, int]], str
]:
    status = parse_name_status(_git(*build_diff_args(base_ref, "HEAD")))
    numstat = parse_numstat(_git("diff", "--numstat", f"{base_ref}...HEAD"))
    diff = _git("diff", "--unified=0", f"{base_ref}...HEAD")
    return status, numstat, diff


def _emit(kind: str, message: str) -> None:
    print(f"::{kind}::{message}")


def _write_warnings(path: str | None, warnings: Sequence[str]) -> None:
    if path:
        Path(path).write_text("\n".join(warnings) + ("\n" if warnings else ""), encoding="utf-8")


def _diff_shape(args: object) -> int:
    config = load_config(Path(args.config))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    allowlist = load_allowlist(Path(args.allowlist))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    base_ref = args.base_ref  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    status, numstat, _diff = _collect(base_ref)
    deleted = [new for change, new, _old in status if change == "D"]
    behind = int(
        (_git("rev-list", "--count", f"HEAD..{base_ref}").strip() or "0")
    )
    result = guard_diff_shape(
        deleted=deleted,
        numstat=numstat,
        allowlist=allowlist,
        config=config,
        release_lookup=_release_lookup(base_ref),
        behind=behind,
    )
    for warning in result.warnings:
        _emit("warning", warning)
    for error in result.errors:
        _emit("error", error)
    if result.failed:
        print(f"pr-guardrails: {len(result.errors)} error(s)")
        return 1
    print("pr-guardrails: diff shape OK")
    return 0


def _body_truth(args: object) -> int:
    config = load_config(Path(args.config))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    base_ref = args.base_ref  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    status, numstat, diff = _collect(base_ref)
    added = parse_added_lines(diff)
    counted = {path: stat for path, stat in numstat.items() if not is_generated(path, config)}
    net_lines = sum(added_lines - deleted_lines for added_lines, deleted_lines in counted.values())
    base_paths = _git("ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", base_ref).splitlines()
    body = Path(args.body_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

    result = check_body_truth(
        body,
        args.title,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        changed_files=len(status),
        tests_added=count_tests_added(added),
        net_lines=net_lines,
        changed_paths=[new for _change, new, _old in status],
        base_paths=base_paths,
        config=config,
    )
    for warning in result.warnings:
        _emit("warning", warning)
    for error in result.errors:
        _emit("error", error)
    _write_warnings(args.warnings_out, result.warnings)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    if result.failed:
        print(f"pr-guardrails: {len(result.errors)} body-truth error(s)")
        return 1
    print("pr-guardrails: body truth OK")
    return 0


def _fabrication(args: object) -> int:
    base_ref = args.base_ref  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    _status, _numstat, diff = _collect(base_ref)
    warnings = check_fabrication(parse_added_lines(diff))
    for warning in warnings:
        _emit("warning", warning)
    _write_warnings(args.warnings_out, warnings)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    print(f"pr-guardrails: {len(warnings)} fabrication warning(s)")
    return 0


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    import argparse

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Deterministic pull request guardrails.")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    common = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)
    common.add_argument("--base-ref", default="origin/main")
    common.add_argument("--config", default=".github/pr-guardrails/config.yml")
    common.add_argument("--allowlist", default=".github/pr-guardrails/deletion-allowlist.yml")

    subparsers.add_parser("diff-shape", parents=[common])

    body_parser = subparsers.add_parser("body-truth", parents=[common])
    body_parser.add_argument("--body-file", required=True)
    body_parser.add_argument("--title", default="")
    body_parser.add_argument("--warnings-out")

    fabrication_parser = subparsers.add_parser("fabrication", parents=[common])
    fabrication_parser.add_argument("--warnings-out")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "diff-shape":
        return _diff_shape(args)
    if args.command == "body-truth":
        return _body_truth(args)
    return _fabrication(args)

name: PR guardrails

# Deterministic gates that a pull request cannot lie about its shape.
# No repository secrets: the gates only need the checked-out repository.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited]

concurrency:
  group: pr-guardrails-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  pr-guardrails:
    name: PR guardrails
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      # Full history so the cumulative base...HEAD diff and release tags exist.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Fetch the base branch
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags origin \
            "${{ github.base_ref }}:refs/remotes/origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

      # The diff-shape gate is the only gate that blocks, and it runs on the
      # cumulative diff: a tree-replacement commit in the middle of a branch
      # stays visible here.
      - name: Diff-shape gate
        if: always()
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py diff-shape \
            --base-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

      - name: Body-truth gate
        if: always()
        env:
          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        run: |
          printf '%s' "$PR_BODY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-body.md"
          uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py body-truth \
            --base-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" \
            --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr-body.md" \
            --title "$PR_TITLE" \
            --warnings-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/body-warnings.txt"

      - name: Fabrication guard
        if: always()
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py fabrication \
            --base-ref "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}" \
            --warnings-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/fabrication-warnings.txt"

      - name: Publish guardrail warnings
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          message="$RUNNER_TEMP/guardrail-warnings.md"
          : > "$message"
          for file in "$RUNNER_TEMP/body-warnings.txt" "$RUNNER_TEMP/fabrication-warnings.txt"; do
            if [ -s "$file" ]; then
              {
                echo "## PR guardrails — warnings"
                echo
                echo '```'
                cat "$file"
                echo '```'
              } >> "$message"
            fi
          done
          if [ -s "$message" ]; then
            gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --body-file "$message" \
              --edit-last --create-if-none ||
              echo "note: could not post the warning comment (fork or token permissions)"
          fi

1:# Repository Architecture
5:## Layout

---
- `packages/core` depends on no other workspace package.
- `packages/connectors` depends on `core` only where it needs shared models.
- Every runnable app may depend on `core`; none of them imports another app.
- The React SPA only talks to `apps/studio-api` over `/api`; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.
- The SPA's conversation runtime is assistant-ui, bound to the Studio's own
  store in `apps/studio/src/assistant/`. That directory
  is the whole bridge: `convert.ts` maps the two message models in both
  directions, `StudioRuntime.tsx` wires the runtime callbacks, and
  `attachments.ts` extracts files in the browser. The library is presentation
  only — it holds no product state and makes no network calls of its own.

## Persistence

- `SQLiteRepository` is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
- The default database is `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`.
- Studio conversation history and PM memory use a separate SQLite database,
  `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`. They are
  sidecar-local and never enter the ODI repository or the MCP contract.
- `build_repository()` chooses SQLite by default and `InMemoryRepository` when `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:`, which is what tests use.
- The CLI selects its backend with `--backend local|mcp` or `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`.
- The Studio API selects `local` (direct service calls) or `mcp` (passthrough) with `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` or `create_app(backend=...)`.

## MCP Contract

`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` owns `ToolName`, `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, and `TOOL_NAMES`. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`; the CLI's local handlers are checked by `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`.

## Entry Points

| Command | Module |
|---|---|
| `agentic-odi` | `agentic_odi_cli.cli:app` |
| `agentic-odi-server` / `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | `agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main` |
| `agentic-odi-studio-api` | `agentic_odi_studio_api.main:main` |
| `uv run python scripts/dev.py` | Dev launcher (MCP + Studio API) |

## Related

- [Data flow](data-flow.md)
- [Testing](testing.md)
- [Decisions (ADRs)](adr/README.md) — why the architecture looks the way it does

## Pull Request Guardrails

`.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml` runs three gates on the cumulative
`base...HEAD` diff, so a tree-replacement commit buried in the middle of a
branch is still visible:

- **diff-shape** (blocking): refuses to delete a file that exists on the base
  branch unless it is listed in `.github/pr-guardrails/deletion-allowlist.yml`;
  refuses a diff that deletes more than `max_deletions` lines or changes more
  than `max_changed_files` files, excluding regenerated files. Thresholds live
  in `.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml`.
- **body-truth** (warns; the fenced JSON diff summary blocks): compares
  natural-language file/test claims and the machine-readable block against the
  real diff.
- **fabrication** (warns): flags new `TODO`/`FIXME`/`NotImplementedError`/stubs,
  unconditional `is_available`, hardcoded measurements, and "mock" returns.

The logic lives in `scripts/pr_guards.py`; the YAML only gathers the diff.
Unit tests are in `tests/scripts/test_pr_guards.py`.

Repository ruleset `main-requires-ci-green` (id `25356329`) requires both
`CI green` and `PR guardrails`, sets
`strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, and keeps the admin bypass only
for pull requests (`bypass_mode: pull_request`). Rulesets are repository
settings, not files; change them with `gh api` and record it here.

def _load_and_validate_presets() -> None:
    """Read connectors.json and validate every preset at import time.

    Exits the process with code 1 if any preset is invalid.
    """
    path = config_path()
    if not path.exists():
        return
    try:
        with path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            payload = json.load(handle)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(f"Error reading connectors config: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    presets = payload.get("connectors", [])
    if not isinstance(presets, list):
        print("Error: connectors config must contain a 'connectors' list", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    bad_presets = []
    for preset in presets:
        try:
            validate_connector_config(preset)
        except ConfigurationError as exc:
            bad_presets.append((preset, exc.keys))

## Summary

A pull request must not be able to lie about its shape or its description. This adds deterministic guardrails that run before a human reads the diff, so a branch that silently deletes shipped files, or a body that claims work it did not do, fails or is annotated by CI.

## What a person experiences

Before reviewing, CI answers two questions: *does this delete anything that is already shipped?* and *does the description match the diff?* A PR that deletes a base-branch file fails with the file name and the release it shipped in. A body whose file/test claims, named files, or JSON summary disagree with the diff gets a warning comment (the JSON block fails).

## What changed

- `scripts/pr_guards.py` — all gate logic, so it is unit-testable:
  - diff-shape: default-deny deletion allowlist, deletion/file budgets with generated-file exclusions, branch-freshness warning, all on the cumulative `base...HEAD` diff;
  - body-truth: file-count, test-count, named-file, and title-number rules (warnings), plus the fenced JSON diff summary (fails on mismatch);
  - fabrication: new TODO/FIXME/NotImplementedError/stub, unconditional `is_available`, hardcoded measurements, and `mock` returns (warnings, tests excluded).
- `.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml` — runs on `pull_request`, full history, fetches the base, needs no repository secrets.
- `.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml` and `deletion-allowlist.yml` — thresholds and an empty (deny-all) allowlist.
- `.github/pull_request_template.md` — experience, verification, scope, diff summary, mock/stub disclosure, and the JSON block.
- `docs/architecture/README.md` — records the ruleset change.
- `tests/scripts/test_pr_guards.py` — one test per rule, including a real git repository proving the cumulative diff catches a mid-branch tree-replacement commit.

## How this was verified

```

  1219 passed, 2 warnings

uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .

uv run mypy apps brand packages

uv run python scripts/pr_guards.py body-truth --base-ref main ...
  ::warning::... claims 7 files, but the diff changes 2
  ::error::The JSON diff summary claims changed_files=7, but the diff has 2
  pr-guardrails: 2 body-truth error(s)   # exit 1
```

## What this does NOT do

- Does not review code quality, and never approves a PR.
- Does not land the six tree-replacement branches' real work (#87).

title:	No surface may lie: label every demo, seed, and simulated signal
state:	OPEN
author:	alehar9320 (Alexander)

> **TL;DR** — The Studio shows you things it made up and never tells you so. Right now a first-time user sees three invented notifications ("Friction Collapse Simulation Complete"), a demo job called "JOB-402 / Sync Environment Secrets", and a Settings panel listing Gong, Slack and telemetry that can never connect — all presented as if they were real. After this issue, every piece of data in the Studio wears a label saying where it came from, demo data is visibly demo data, anything simulated is visibly simulated, and the two surfaces that pretend to be connected are either made real or removed. Nothing else about the product changes.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/studio` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | — |
| **Related PRs** | #63, #65, #66, #70 |
| **Blocks** | #79, #81, #95 |

---

## The problem

The Living Studio is a product where a person states intent and the system returns signals. That contract only works if every signal is real. Today it is not.

**1. Seed data is served as production data.** When the MCP server is unreachable or returns no jobs, `fetch_canvas` returns the demo seed:

- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/mcp_data.py:31` and `:82` — `seed_payload()` is returned when MCP is unreachable or empty.
- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/seed.py:1-101` — the seed is a fictional product, a fictional job (`JOB-402`, "Sync Environment Secrets Across Microservices"), fictional outcomes with fabricated importance/satisfaction numbers.
- The projection already carries the truth: the payload includes `"source": "seed"` and the SPA type declares it (`apps/studio/src/types.ts:27-32`). **Nothing in the UI ever reads it.**

**2. The "Catch Up" feed is fed by a demo button.** `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:402-433` — `simulateBackgroundEvent` picks one of three hardcoded strings at random and pushes it as a notification. It is wired to a button literally labelled **"+ Simulate update"** (`apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx:127-134`). There is no `/api/notifications` route, no server-side event source, no polling, no SSE subscription outside the chat request, and no connector path that produces a notification.

**3. A first-time user is shown fabricated activity as history.** `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:79-113` — `SEED_NOTIFICATIONS` contains three invented notifications, including "Friction Collapse Simulation Complete" and "New Customer Telemetry Signal". They are loaded whenever `localStorage` has no `studio.notifications` key (`:250-260`). The README tells the user to *"use the bell to catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away"* — which is exactly the fabrication.

**4. Settings lists three integrations that can never be connected.** `apps/studio/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:134-148` — "Gong transcripts", "Slack friction stream", and "Product telemetry" are static list items with a permanent `status-dot is-unknown`. They are not the real connector presets (`packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/catalog.py:236` lists 16 real presets), so a person reading Settings cannot tell which integrations are actually available.

**5. The docs describe the stub as shipped.** `docs/architecture/notifications.md:1-6` is titled *"Memory Recording for Notification/Alert System in Studio"* and lists what was "added". It never says the feed is seeded and simulated. `docs/living-studio.md:45,47` documents the catch-up bar button and lens as if a real signal system exists.

**6. The agent can render a card whose numbers are invented.** `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx:176-227` — the `impact-simulation` card takes `before[]`, `after[]`, `metrics[]`, and `verdict` entirely as `props`. There is no Bet/Simulation entity, no MCP tool, and no computation anywhere in the repository. Whatever the model writes is displayed as a measured before/after. The catalog even advertises it as *"a before/after simulation of a bet"* (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:198-203`).

**7. A non-existent feature is advertised on the public site.** `website/tools/sync-readme.py:254` renders a "Causal Lineage" mention into the site copy. There is no lineage model, tool, or graph in the repository.

## What a person experiences

A person opens the Studio for the first time. Instead of a wall of invented activity, they see the empty product, and a single honest line: *"No opportunities yet. Tell me the job your customers are trying to get done."* If the backend is unreachable, a persistent amber strip says **"Demo data — the ODI server is not reachable"** and every card carries a `DEMO` chip. If a person deliberately asks the agent to *simulate* an impact bet, the simulation card is rendered with a visible **"Simulated — no model behind this number"** ribbon, and the numbers are never presented as measurements. The Settings panel lists the sixteen connectors that actually exist and connects to them, and the three rows that never could connect are gone. Nothing in the Studio asserts something the system does not know.

## Specification

### 1.1 Provenance on the canvas projection

Extend the canvas payload with an explicit, machine-readable provenance object, and make the SPA render it.

**Backend** — `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/mcp_data.py`:

- `fetch_canvas` and `fetch_local_canvas` must both return a `provenance` object:

```python
{
    "kind": "live" | "seed" | "empty",
    "reason": str | None,        # e.g. "mcp_unreachable", "no_jobs", "local_store_empty"
    "generated_at": str,          # ISO-8601 UTC
    "record_counts": {"jobs": int, "steps": int, "outcomes": int, "evidence": int},
}
```

- `kind` is `"live"` only when the read came from the repository. It is `"seed"` only when `seed_payload()` was substituted, and `reason` must then be non-null. It is `"empty"` when the repository is genuinely empty — **this is a distinct, non-ugly state and must never be confused with an error**.
- Keep the existing top-level `"source"` key for backward compatibility for one release, but derive it from `provenance.kind` rather than setting it independently.

**Frontend** — `apps/studio/src/types.ts`:

- Add `provenance: CanvasProvenance` to `CanvasData`.
- `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkbenchRail.tsx:26-60` — render a persistent `DEMO` / `OFFLINE` chip in the rail header whenever `provenance.kind !== "live"`. The chip is not dismissible while the condition holds.
- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx` — when `provenance.kind === "seed"`, render an inline banner above the matrix: *"Demo data. Nothing here comes from your research."* with a link to Settings → Connectors.

### 1.2 Seeded notifications must be labeled and separable

**Frontend** — `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:79-113`:

- Add `simulated: boolean` to the `StudioNotification` type (`apps/studio/src/types.ts:88-104`).
- `SEED_NOTIFICATIONS` entries are `simulated: true` and their `source` is `"demo"`.
- The simulator (`StudioContext.tsx:402-433`) produces `simulated: true` entries with `source: "simulator"`.
- **Do not seed the feed on first run.** Replace the seed load (`StudioContext.tsx:250-260`) with an empty feed plus a single honest empty state.
- `apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx:197-204` — the empty state copy must say plainly that nothing has happened yet, and must not imply a backlog.

### 1.3 The simulator must be unmistakably a simulator

- `apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx:127-134` — the "+ Simulate update" button stays (it is a legitimate developer affordance) but every notification it creates renders a **"Simulated"** badge (`simulated === true`), and simulated notifications are visually distinct (a dashed border, a muted palette) and are excluded from the "While you were away" executive summary counters.
- Simulated notifications must never be persisted as if they were real: when writing to `localStorage`, either omit them or write them with `simulated: true` and filter them out of the unread count.

### 1.4 Settings must list what actually exists

- `apps/studio/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:134-148` — **delete** the three hardcoded rows ("Gong transcripts", "Slack friction stream", "Product telemetry").
- Replace them with a real list rendered from `GET /api/connectors/catalog` (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:95-97`), grouped by the five `CapabilityArea` values from `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/catalog.py:19-33`. Each row shows the preset id, its auth type (`token` / `oauth` / `none`), and a connect affordance that uses the existing `POST /api/connectors` route (`router.py:109-117`).
- If the catalog request fails, render an explicit error row — not an empty `<select>` (see #91).

### 1.5 The impact-simulation card must declare itself

- `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx:176-227` — the `impact-simulation` card must accept and require a `provenance` prop with one of `"simulated" | "measured"`. `"measured"` is only legal if a real computation backs it; until #95 lands there is no such computation, so **the only legal value today is `"simulated"`**.
- `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` — add `provenance` to the card's required props so the server-side validator (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/ui_spec.py:106-155`) rejects a card that omits it. A model that renders an impact simulation without declaring it simulated is rejected and asked to fix it, exactly like the existing `render_ui` validation-failure path (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:332-340`).
- The card renders a **"Simulated"** ribbon. The word "measured", "actual", or "observed" must never appear without a real data source.

### 1.6 Documentation must describe what ships

- `docs/architecture/notifications.md` — rewrite. It must state, in one sentence, that the catch-up feed's content is currently produced by a local simulator, and point at the issue that replaces it.
- `docs/living-studio.md:45,47` — add the same caveat to the catch-up description.
- `website/tools/sync-readme.py:254` — remove the "Causal Lineage" claim unless a lineage surface exists.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **No surface may assert data the system did not read.** If a value did not come from the repository, from a connector, or from a computation the system performed, it must be labeled as a simulation or removed.
- **Do not delete the simulator.** It is a useful developer affordance. Relabel it; do not remove it.

## Triage — scope, non-goals, and acceptance criteria

**Scope** — Make the three surfaces that currently present invented data as real wear an explicit, machine-readable origin, and make the docs/site describe what ships. Concretely: (a) add a `provenance` object (`kind` = `live` | `seed` | `empty`, `reason`, `generated_at`, `record_counts`) to the canvas projection from both `fetch_canvas` and `fetch_local_canvas`, and render it in the SPA; (b) label the notification feed and the simulator as simulated and stop seeding the feed on first run; (c) require a `provenance` prop on the `impact-simulation` card, enforced by the server-side UI validator; (d) correct the doc and site claims about the catch-up feed and Causal Lineage. Files: `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/{mcp_data,seed,ui_spec,router}.py`, `apps/studio/src/{types.ts,state/StudioContext.tsx,components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx,components/SettingsPanel.tsx,components/workspace/WorkbenchRail.tsx,components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx,ui/cards.tsx,ui/catalog.ts}`, `docs/architecture/notifications.md`, `docs/living-studio.md`, and the website build inputs. Verified against current `main` (`1da2713`, 0.12.0). Note: the hardcoded Settings rows named in the issue were already removed by #134 (`feb465a`), and the referenced `website/tools/sync-readme.py` does not exist — the live claim is `docs/living-studio.md:5` published through `website/content/nav.json` / `website/tools/build_site.py`.

**Non-goals** — Building the real signal system (#79); computing impact simulations for real (#95); persisting the conversation (#81); any ODI data-model or schema migration; changing the agent system prompt (`chat.py` `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, owned separately); letting the SPA contact MCP or the LLM directly; replacing assistant-ui or the render bridge; removing the simulator (it is relabelled, not deleted); and the sixteen-preset catalog is not re-authored here, only surfaced from the existing `/api/connectors/catalog`.

**Acceptance criteria** —
- `GET /api/canvas` returns a `provenance` object with `kind`, `reason`, `generated_at`, and `record_counts` on both the MCP and local backends; `kind == "seed"` implies `reason != null`; `kind == "live"` occurs only when the payload was read from the repository; a genuinely empty repository yields `kind == "empty"` and is not treated as an error.
- The top-level `source` key is still present and is derived from `provenance.kind` (backward compatible for one release).
- The SPA renders a non-dismissible `DEMO`/`OFFLINE` chip in the workbench rail whenever `provenance.kind != "live"`, and an inline demo banner above the opportunity landscape when `kind == "seed"`.
- On first run with no `studio.notifications` key, the feed is empty and its empty state does not imply a backlog; `SEED_NOTIFICATIONS` is not loaded as history.
- `StudioNotification` carries `simulated: boolean`; simulated entries render a visible "Simulated" badge, are visually distinct, are excluded from the "While you were away" counters and the unread badge, and are not persisted as if real (omitted, or stored with `simulated: true` and filtered out of the unread count).
- `SettingsPanel` lists the real presets from `GET /api/connectors/catalog` grouped by the five `CapabilityArea` values, each row showing the preset id, its auth type (`token`/`oauth`/`none`), and a connect affordance using `POST /api/connectors`; a failed catalog fetch renders an explicit error row rather than an empty `<select>`.
- `impact-simulation` requires a `provenance` prop whose only legal value today is `"simulated"`; the server-side validator rejects a spec that omits it and the model is asked to fix it on the same turn; the card renders a visible "Simulated" ribbon and never uses "measured"/"actual"/"observed" without a real source.
- `docs/architecture/notifications.md` states in one sentence that the catch-up feed is currently produced by a local simulator and names the issue that replaces it; `docs/living-studio.md` carries the same caveat; the published site copy no longer advertises "Causal Lineage" while no lineage surface exists.
- The OpenAPI schema and `apps/studio/src/api/schema.d.ts` are regenerated and CI's "Verify generated API types are up to date" step passes.
- Failure, compatibility, and cleanup cases: MCP unreachable ⇒ `kind == "seed"`, `reason == "mcp_unreachable"`; partial hydration (some tool calls fail) must not silently upgrade provenance to `live` and must keep its warnings; a cached canvas payload from an older client that lacks `provenance` must not be treated as live; `fetch_local_canvas` returns `empty` for an empty local store; no new secrets are introduced and all SPA reads stay behind the sidecar.

"""MCP hydration and passthrough writes, ported from the Streamlit app."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
from typing import Any

from agentic_odi_core import ODIService, ToolName
from agentic_odi_core.remote import (
    StudioError,
    StudioErrorCode,
    parse_tool_result,
    tool_result_text,
)
from fastmcp import Client as McpClient
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError

from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.errors import StudioHTTPError
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.probes import is_endpoint_reachable
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.seed import seed_payload

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT = 3.0


async def fetch_canvas(mcp_url: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch live canvas data from FastMCP, falling back to the seed prototype."""
    jobs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    evidence: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []

    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        log.warning("MCP endpoint unreachable at %s — falling back to seed data", mcp_url)
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["MCP endpoint unreachable"]}

    try:
        mcp_client = McpClient(mcp_url)
        async with mcp_client:
            raw_jobs = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOBS.value, {}), timeout=1.5
            )
            try:
                parsed_jobs = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_jobs))
                if isinstance(parsed_jobs, list):
                    jobs = parsed_jobs
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                log.warning("Failed to parse jobs from MCP: %s", exc)
                jobs = []

            for job in jobs:
                job_id = job.get("id")
                if not job_id:
                    continue

                try:
                    raw_steps = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOB_MAP.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_steps = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_steps))
                    if isinstance(parsed_steps, list):
                        steps.extend(parsed_steps)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch steps for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)

                try:
                    raw_outcomes = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_OUTCOMES.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_outcomes = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_outcomes))
                    if isinstance(parsed_outcomes, list):
                        outcomes.extend(parsed_outcomes)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch outcomes for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)

            try:
                raw_evidence = await asyncio.wait_for(
                    mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.LIST_EVIDENCE.value, {}), timeout=1.0
                )
                parsed_evidence = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_evidence))
                if isinstance(parsed_evidence, list):
                    evidence = parsed_evidence
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                msg = f"Failed to fetch evidence: {exc}"
                log.warning(msg)
                warnings.append(msg)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        log.warning("MCP canvas hydration failed entirely: %s", exc)
        warnings.append(f"MCP hydration error: {exc}")

    if not jobs:
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["No jobs returned from MCP"]}

    return {
        "jobs": jobs,
        "steps": steps,
        "outcomes": outcomes,
        "evidence": evidence,
        "source": "mcp",
        "warnings": warnings,
    }


def fetch_local_canvas(service: ODIService) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read the canvas directly from the local service, no HTTP round trip."""
    jobs = [job.model_dump() for job in service.get_jobs()]
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for job in jobs:
        job_id = job["id"]
        steps.extend(step.model_dump() for step in service.get_job_map(job_id))
        outcomes.extend(outcome.model_dump() for outcome in service.get_outcomes(job_id))
    evidence = [item.model_dump() for item in service.list_evidence()]
    return {
        "jobs": jobs,
        "steps": steps,
        "outcomes": outcomes,
        "evidence": evidence,
        "source": "local",
    }

"""Tests for MCP hydration and passthrough helpers."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Any

import pytest
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio import mcp_data
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.errors import StudioHTTPError


class _FakeClient:
    payloads: dict[str, Any] = {}
    error: Exception | None = None
    calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []

    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
        self.url = url

    async def __aenter__(self) -> _FakeClient:
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc: Any) -> bool:
        return False

    async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
        self.calls.append((name, arguments))
        if self.error is not None:
            raise self.error
        payload = str(self.payloads.get(name, "[]"))
        # FastMCP hands back a CallToolResult, whose str() is a repr.
        return SimpleNamespace(content=[SimpleNamespace(text=payload)])


def test_fetch_canvas_falls_back_to_seed_when_unreachable(monkeypatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: False)

    payload = asyncio.run(mcp_data.fetch_canvas("http://mcp"))

    assert payload["source"] == "seed"
    assert payload["jobs"][0]["id"] == "JOB-402"


def test_fetch_canvas_hydrates_jobs_steps_and_outcomes(monkeypatch) -> None:
    _FakeClient.calls = []
    _FakeClient.error = None
    _FakeClient.payloads = {
        "get_jobs": json.dumps([{"id": "job-1"}]),
        "get_job_map": json.dumps([{"id": "step-1", "job_id": "job-1"}]),
        "get_outcomes": json.dumps([{"id": "outcome-1", "job_id": "job-1"}]),
        "list_evidence": json.dumps([{"id": "evidence-1", "job_id": "job-1"}]),
    }
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "McpClient", _FakeClient)

    payload = asyncio.run(mcp_data.fetch_canvas("http://mcp"))

    assert payload == {
        "jobs": [{"id": "job-1"}],
        "steps": [{"id": "step-1", "job_id": "job-1"}],
        "outcomes": [{"id": "outcome-1", "job_id": "job-1"}],
        "evidence": [{"id": "evidence-1", "job_id": "job-1"}],
        "source": "mcp",
        "warnings": [],
    }
    assert _FakeClient.calls == [
        ("get_jobs", {}),
        ("get_job_map", {"job_id": "job-1"}),
        ("get_outcomes", {"job_id": "job-1"}),
        ("list_evidence", {}),
    ]


def test_fetch_canvas_skips_invalid_json_and_jobs_without_ids(monkeypatch) -> None:
    _FakeClient.calls = []
    _FakeClient.error = None
    _FakeClient.payloads = {"get_jobs": "not json"}
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "McpClient", _FakeClient)

    payload = asyncio.run(mcp_data.fetch_canvas("http://mcp"))

    assert payload["source"] == "seed"

    _FakeClient.payloads = {"get_jobs": json.dumps([{"name": "no id"}])}
    payload = asyncio.run(mcp_data.fetch_canvas("http://mcp"))

    # Entries without an id are skipped, so no per-job lookups happen.
    assert payload["source"] == "mcp"
    assert payload["steps"] == []
    assert payload["outcomes"] == []
    assert _FakeClient.calls == [
        ("get_jobs", {}),
        ("list_evidence", {}),
        ("get_jobs", {}),
        ("list_evidence", {}),
    ]


def test_call_mcp_tool_rejects_unreachable_endpoints(monkeypatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: False)

    with pytest.raises(StudioHTTPError) as exc_info:
        asyncio.run(mcp_data.call_mcp_tool("http://mcp", "get_jobs", {}))

    assert exc_info.value.status_code == 502
    assert exc_info.value.error.code.value == "mcp_unreachable"
    assert exc_info.value.error.retryable is True
    assert "unreachable" in exc_info.value.error.message.lower()


def test_call_mcp_tool_returns_the_result_text(monkeypatch) -> None:
    _FakeClient.calls = []
    _FakeClient.error = None
    _FakeClient.payloads = {"get_jobs": "[]"}
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "McpClient", _FakeClient)

    result = asyncio.run(mcp_data.call_mcp_tool("http://mcp", "get_jobs", {}))

    assert result == "[]"
    assert _FakeClient.calls == [("get_jobs", {})]


def test_call_mcp_tool_reads_the_text_of_a_call_tool_result(monkeypatch) -> None:
    class _ResultClient(_FakeClient):
        async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
            return SimpleNamespace(
                content=[SimpleNamespace(text='Outcome created successfully: {"id": "O-1"}')]
            )

    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "McpClient", _ResultClient)

    result = asyncio.run(mcp_data.call_mcp_tool("http://mcp", "add_outcome", {}))

    assert result == 'Outcome created successfully: {"id": "O-1"}'


def test_call_mcp_tool_raises_a_typed_error_for_an_error_text(monkeypatch) -> None:
    class _ResultClient(_FakeClient):
        async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
            return SimpleNamespace(
                content=[SimpleNamespace(text="Error: Job with ID JOB-1 not found.")]
            )

    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "McpClient", _ResultClient)

    with pytest.raises(StudioHTTPError) as exc_info:
        asyncio.run(mcp_data.call_mcp_tool("http://mcp", "get_job", {}))

    assert exc_info.value.status_code == 404
    assert exc_info.value.error.code.value == "not_found"


def test_call_mcp_tool_wraps_client_errors(monkeypatch) -> None:
    _FakeClient.calls = []
    _FakeClient.error = RuntimeError("boom")
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "McpClient", _FakeClient)

    with pytest.raises(StudioHTTPError) as exc_info:
        asyncio.run(mcp_data.call_mcp_tool("http://mcp", "get_jobs", {}))

    assert exc_info.value.status_code == 502
    assert exc_info.value.error.code.value == "mcp_unreachable"
    assert exc_info.value.error.retryable is True
    assert "Error calling get_jobs: boom" in exc_info.value.error.message


def test_fetch_canvas_reports_why_the_seed_is_standing_in(monkeypatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: False)

    payload = asyncio.run(mcp_data.fetch_canvas("http://mcp"))

    assert payload["source"] == "seed"
    assert payload["warnings"] == ["MCP endpoint unreachable"]


def test_call_mcp_tool_reports_a_tool_error_as_a_tool_failure(monkeypatch) -> None:
    from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError

    class _FailingClient(_FakeClient):
        async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
            raise ToolError("the tool refused")

    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "McpClient", _FailingClient)

    with pytest.raises(StudioHTTPError) as exc_info:
        asyncio.run(mcp_data.call_mcp_tool("http://mcp", "add_job", {}))

    assert exc_info.value.status_code == 500
    assert exc_info.value.error.code.value == "mcp_tool_failed"

> **TL;DR** — Six of the seven open pull requests on this repository contain a single commit that quietly replaces the whole tree with an old snapshot, deleting nine to eleven features that were already merged. They pass CI, because the reverted tree is internally consistent. Their descriptions are also materially false — one claims "20 touch-first improvements" and ships three CSS blocks and five tests; another claims to "delegate knowledge storage to external systems" and adds a URL field. After this issue, a pull request that deletes a file that exists on `main`, or whose description does not match its diff, fails CI before a human ever reads it.
