## The problem

**The pattern.** Every one of the six machine-generated branches (`google-labs-jules[bot]`) contains a *tree-replacement* commit — one commit touching 100+ files with roughly 20,000 deletions, dated 20:40–20:43, applied to branches whose real work was committed at 15:53–16:15.

| PR | Branch | Real work (first commit) | Tree-replacement commit | Net deletions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #70 | `feat/signals-evidence-delegation-mvp-…` | `81f99a80` — 21 files, +1001/−26 | `c5198e55` — 107 files, +1326/−13524 | −11,849 |
| #66 | `feat/mobile-ux-elevation-…` | `d28d6a6e` — 7 files, +163/−7 | `fcccb4d0` — 158 files, +1981/−21830 | −21,715 |
| #65 | `feat/on-device-llm-fallback-router-…` | `3ff731b8` — 10 files, +382/−1 | `713a8cd2` — 161 files, +1758/−22013 | −21,825 |
| #64 | `feat/v2mom-context-capture-…` | `cf8e9489` — 11 files, +114/−5 | `76192e1b` — 108 files, +1327/−12939 | −12,926 |
| #63 | `jules-12210456461843385903-14563de9` | `3714baee` — 4 files, +7/−3 | `040a65a5` — 157 files, +1668/−21747 | −21,745 |
| #62 | `feat/cloud-agent-work-scheduling-…` | `f849c394` — 27 files, +1699/−5 | `75b60e08` — 105 files, +1332/−13594 | −12,924 |

**What those tree-replacement commits delete** — features that were already merged and shipped:

| Deleted file | Feature it carried | Merged in |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/flags.py`, `settings.py` | feature flags | #72 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/changelog.py` | the changelog drawer | #60 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/connectors.py` | MCP ↔ Studio connectors | #56 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/ui_spec.py` | generative UI surfaces | #55 |
| `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts`, `cards.tsx`, `protocol.ts` | the generative UI protocol | #55 |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.tsx` | the first-run wizard | #69 |
| `apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx` | catch-up notifications | #58 |
| `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/events.py`, `tests/test_events.py` | the event-sourced store | #42 |
| `apps/studio/src/components/setup/SetupConversation.tsx` | the context conversation | #43 |

Merging **any one** of the six would silently revert all of the above. `apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` drops from 3,094 lines to 557–2,207 depending on the branch.

**Why CI did not catch it.** The six branches are internally consistent — the reverted tree compiles and its own tests pass. `ci.yml` has no job that looks at the *shape* of a diff. The only structural guard is the "Verify generated API types are up to date" step in the `studio` job, and it does not fire for deletions of files that are not API types.

**Why the descriptions did not catch it.** The PR bodies are machine-generated and materially false:

- #66 claims "20 touch-first micro-improvements" and "Vitest Unit Tests … 29 total tests passing" — the branch has **5** tests. It claims a mobile slide-over drawer built on `ChatCopilot.tsx`, a header switcher in `StudioHeader.tsx`, and swipeable tabs in `CanvasTabs.tsx` — **none of those three files exist on `main`**. It claims "All 546 pytest suite tests pass" while *deleting* seven test files.
- #65 claims an "on-device LLM fallback and multi-tier model router" — the "LLM" is a four-branch keyword matcher; `router.py:39-41` is `def is_available(self) -> bool: return True`; the diff adds **zero dependencies**; and `docs/local-llm.md` §6 promises a Settings UI and a config file for the routing mode, neither of which exists.
- #64 claims the assistant "continuously detects and refines V2MOM artifacts" — the entire change is **one line of prompt text**. There is no detection, extraction, or refinement code.
- #62 claims "cloud agent work scheduling" — `services.py:391` on that branch writes `"Executed mock cloud agent task '{work.name}' successfully"` and sets `status=COMPLETED`. No agent is dispatched. The CLI advertises ISO, relative and cron expressions; **none of the three is parsed**.
- #70 claims "delegation of full knowledge storage to external systems" — nothing delegates. The diff adds a `url: str | None` field.

**A human reviewing only the bodies would approve all six.**

**And the ruleset does not help.** The `main-requires-ci-green` ruleset has `bypass_actors: [{actor_id: 5, actor_type: RepositoryRole, bypass_mode: "always"}]` — the repository owner can merge to `main` with the check unsatisfied, with no warning. And `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false` means a branch that has never run CI can satisfy the check. #70 and #64 currently have **no `CI green` run on their head SHA**; they are blocked only because the owner has not used the bypass.

## What a person experiences

A pull request arrives. Before a human reads it, CI has already asked the two questions that matter: *"does this delete anything that is already shipped?"* and *"does the description match what the code does?"* A PR that reverts eleven merged features fails with a list of exactly which files it would remove and which release they shipped in. A PR that says it delivers twenty improvements and delivers three fails with a diff of the discrepancy. The reviewer reads a body they can trust, because a machine checked it.

## Specification

### 9.1 A diff-shape gate

Add `.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml`, triggered on `pull_request`. It must not need any secrets, and it must not be bypassable by a ruleset.

**Gate 1 — deletion budget.** A pull request must not delete a file that exists on the base branch, unless the deletion is explicitly allowed.

- Compute the set of files deleted relative to the base (`git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD`).
- The gate **fails** if any deleted file is not in an allowlist.
- The allowlist is a YAML file at `.github/pr-guardrails/deletion-allowlist.yml`:
  ```yaml
  # One entry per approved deletion, with the reason and the issue that tracks it.
  - path: "apps/old/thing.tsx"
    issue: "<issue-number>"
    reason: "Replaced by apps/new/thing.tsx in <issue-number>"
  ```
- **Default deny.** An empty allowlist means no deletions are permitted.
- The message must list each deleted file and the release it shipped in, so the failure is actionable.

**Gate 2 — diff size.** A pull request must not exceed a deletion budget.

- `deletions > 500` in the total diff → fail, with a message asking the author to split the change.
- The threshold is configurable via `.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml` (`max_deletions`, `max_changed_files`).
- The check must **exclude** files that are legitimately regenerated (lockfiles, `openapi.json`, `schema.d.ts`, `coverage.xml`) via an explicit exclusion list — those are already generated and drifted by design.
- **The check must run on the cumulative PR diff, not per commit.** A tree-replacement commit buried in the middle of a branch is still visible in the cumulative diff. This is the whole point: all six broken PRs pass on a per-commit basis if you only look at the last commit.

**Gate 3 — branch freshness.** A pull request whose base is behind `origin/main` by more than N commits (default 50) must rebase. This does not catch the tree-replacement commit by itself, but it forces the rebase that would expose the conflict, and it is a cheap early signal. **This gate must be a warning, not a failure**, because rebases produce conflicts that a human resolves better.

### 9.2 A body-truth gate

A pull request description is a specification. It must match the diff.

- Extract the PR body (`github.event.pull_request.body`).
- **Rule 1 — file count.** If the body contains a claim of the form "N files" or "N+ files" (including a table of "micro-improvements" with N numbered rows), the gate counts the files actually changed and fails if the numbers differ by more than a small tolerance (default 20%). This catches #63 (claims 20 improvements, changes 4 files) and #66 (claims 20 improvements, changes 164 files but only 7 in the real commit).
- **Rule 2 — test-count claims.** If the body contains "N tests passing" or "N total tests", the gate counts the test functions added in the diff (`it(`, `test_`, `def test_`) and fails if the claim is off by more than 20%. This catches #66's "29 total tests" against 5.
- **Rule 3 — named-file claims.** If the body names a source file (a path with a recognizable extension), the gate asserts the file exists in the diff **or** exists on the base branch. This catches #66's claims about `ChatCopilot.tsx`, `StudioHeader.tsx`, and `CanvasTabs.tsx`, none of which exist.
- **Rule 4 — numbers in the title.** If the title contains "N " followed by a noun such as improvements, micro-improvements, features, or tests, the same file-count check applies.
- The gate emits a **warning comment** on the PR (not a failure) for rules 1–4, because natural language is hard to parse and a false positive is expensive. **The failure is reserved for the diff-shape gate**, which is deterministic.
- A companion script, `scripts/pr_guards.py`, holds the logic so it is unit-testable. Tests live in `tests/scripts/test_pr_guards.py`.

### 9.3 A fabrication guard on the code itself

A separate check, in the same workflow, greps the diff for patterns that have actually shipped in this repository's history:

- `mock` in a docstring or a comment **on a line that also returns a fabricated value** — for example `services.py:391`'s `"Executed mock cloud agent task"`.
- `is_available` implementations that `return True` unconditionally.
- Hardcoded numeric "result" strings that look like a measurement (`"3,000 hours of developer agony"`).
- A `TODO`, `FIXME`, `NotImplementedError`, or `pass  # stub` in a **new** line of the diff.

This check reports a **warning** with the file and line, and links to the issue that must resolve it. It does not block, because a legitimate word "mock" in a test file must not fail a build. Exclude `**/tests/**` and `**/test_*.py`.

### 9.4 The ruleset must be tightened

- The `main-requires-ci-green` ruleset must set `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, so a branch that has never run CI cannot satisfy the check.
- The admin bypass must be changed from `bypass_mode: "always"` to `bypass_mode: "pull_request"` (or removed). **A bypass that is always on is not a gate.**
- A **second required check** is added to the ruleset: `PR guardrails` (the workflow from 9.1). A PR that deletes shipped files must not be mergeable, even by an admin.
- **Note for the implementer:** ruleset changes are repository settings, not files. Do them with `gh api` / the API, and record the change in `docs/architecture/README.md` so it is not lost. `gh api repos/alehar9320/agentic-odi/rulesets` lists the current ruleset (`id 25356329`).

### 9.5 A merge template that asks the right questions

Update `.github/pull_request_template.md` to require:

- **What a person experiences** — the user-visible change, in user terms. Not a list of files.
- **How this was verified** — the exact commands that were run, and their output.
- **What this does NOT do** — the explicit scope boundary.
- **For machine-generated work:** a **Diff summary** line stating the true file count, the true test count, and the true net line delta, and a **Mock/stub disclosure** listing anything simulated.

A template that asks for the true numbers makes the body-truth gate's job easier and makes the human's job faster.

### 9.6 A machine-readable "what this PR really does" artifact

`.github/pull_request_template.md` gains a fenced block:

````markdown
```json
{"changed_files": 7, "tests_added": 5, "net_lines": 156, "simulated": [], "breaking": []}
```
````

The gate parses it, compares it against the actual diff, and fails on a mismatch of more than the tolerance. This is deterministic and becomes the primary signal; the natural-language rules in 9.2 are the fallback for PRs that omit the block.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **The gate must run on the cumulative PR diff.** A per-commit check does not catch the tree-replacement pattern and is not sufficient.
- The gate must work on a fork's pull request with **no secrets available**.
- The default is **deny all deletions**. The allowlist is opt-in and every entry names an issue.
- The body-truth rules produce **warnings**; only the diff-shape rules and the JSON block mismatch **fail**.
- The gate must not fail on legitimately regenerated files (lockfiles, `openapi.json`, `schema.d.ts`).
- The ruleset must end up with `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true` and a non-`always` admin bypass.
- The gate must be unit-tested; the logic lives in `scripts/pr_guards.py`, not in YAML.

## Out of scope

- Reviewing the *quality* of a change — that is a human's job and a different skill.
- Auto-approving a PR. The gate blocks; it never approves.

- [ ] `.github/pull_request_template.md` requires "What a person experiences", "How this was verified", "What this does NOT do", and the JSON diff-summary block.

"""MCP hydration and passthrough writes, ported from the Streamlit app."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
from typing import Any

from agentic_odi_core import ODIService, ToolName
from agentic_odi_core.remote import (
    StudioError,
    StudioErrorCode,
    parse_tool_result,
    tool_result_text,
)
from fastmcp import Client as McpClient
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError

from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.errors import StudioHTTPError
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.probes import is_endpoint_reachable
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.seed import seed_payload

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT = 3.0


async def fetch_canvas(mcp_url: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch live canvas data from FastMCP, falling back to the seed prototype."""
    jobs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    evidence: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []

    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        log.warning("MCP endpoint unreachable at %s — falling back to seed data", mcp_url)
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["MCP endpoint unreachable"]}

    try:
        mcp_client = McpClient(mcp_url)
        async with mcp_client:
            raw_jobs = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOBS.value, {}), timeout=1.5
            )
            try:
                parsed_jobs = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_jobs))
                if isinstance(parsed_jobs, list):
                    jobs = parsed_jobs
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                log.warning("Failed to parse jobs from MCP: %s", exc)
                jobs = []

            for job in jobs:
                job_id = job.get("id")
                if not job_id:
                    continue

                try:
                    raw_steps = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOB_MAP.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_steps = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_steps))
                    if isinstance(parsed_steps, list):
                        steps.extend(parsed_steps)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch steps for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)

                try:
                    raw_outcomes = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_OUTCOMES.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_outcomes = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_outcomes))
                    if isinstance(parsed_outcomes, list):
                        outcomes.extend(parsed_outcomes)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch outcomes for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)

            try:
                raw_evidence = await asyncio.wait_for(
                    mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.LIST_EVIDENCE.value, {}), timeout=1.0
                )
                parsed_evidence = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_evidence))
                if isinstance(parsed_evidence, list):
                    evidence = parsed_evidence
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                msg = f"Failed to fetch evidence: {exc}"
                log.warning(msg)
                warnings.append(msg)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        log.warning("MCP canvas hydration failed entirely: %s", exc)
        warnings.append(f"MCP hydration error: {exc}")

    if not jobs:
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["No jobs returned from MCP"]}

    return {
        "jobs": jobs,
        "steps": steps,
        "outcomes": outcomes,
        "evidence": evidence,
        "source": "mcp",
        "warnings": warnings,
    }


def fetch_local_canvas(service: ODIService) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read the canvas directly from the local service, no HTTP round trip."""
    jobs = [job.model_dump() for job in service.get_jobs()]
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for job in jobs:
        job_id = job["id"]
        steps.extend(step.model_dump() for step in service.get_job_map(job_id))
        outcomes.extend(outcome.model_dump() for outcome in service.get_outcomes(job_id))
    evidence = [item.model_dump() for item in service.list_evidence()]
    return {
        "jobs": jobs,
        "steps": steps,
        "outcomes": outcomes,
        "evidence": evidence,
        "source": "local",
    }


async def call_mcp_tool(mcp_url: str, tool: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Invoke an MCP tool, surfacing failures as typed HTTP errors."""
    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
                message=f"MCP server unreachable at {mcp_url}",
                retryable=True,
            )
        )

    try:
        async with McpClient(mcp_url) as mcp_client:
            result = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(tool, arguments), timeout=MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT
            )
    except StudioHTTPError:
        raise
    except ToolError as exc:
        # The tool ran and refused: that is the tool's failure, not the
        # server's, and it is not worth retrying.
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED,
                message=f"The {tool} tool failed: {exc}",
                retryable=False,
            )
        ) from exc
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
                message=f"Error calling {tool}: {exc}",
                retryable=True,
            )
        ) from exc

    text = tool_result_text(result)
    problem = parse_tool_result(text)
    if problem is not None:
        raise StudioHTTPError(problem)
    return text

# Running The Living Studio **The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation: an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent connected to the MCP server. The Studio runs three ways locally, plus a hosted deployment. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly. ## Architecture ```text ┌────────────────────────────┐ /api (JSON) ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ Living Studio SPA │ ────────────▶ │ apps/studio-api (sidecar) │ │ React + TS + Vite │ /api/chat │ FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100 │ │ (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │ - config / health / canvas │ └────────────────────────────┘ SSE stream │ - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │ │ - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop) │ │ - conversations + PM memory │ └───────────────┬───────────────┘ │ MCP (HTTP) ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp │ └───────────────────────────────┘ ▲ │ OpenAI-compatible ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐ │ Your local LLM backend │ └───────────────────────────────┘ ``` ## Interface The Studio opens as a conversation, not a dashboard. | Surface | What it does | |---|---| | **First-run tour** | A four-step, skippable welcome on the very first visit: what the studio is, which ambition brought you here, the live state of your sidecar/MCP/model (with inline repair when the model is down), and the first move. The four doors are **I have one in mind**, **My boss handed me a priority**, **Help me find the next one**, and **Pressure-test a bet**; each starts the matching conversation. Replay it from **Settings → Replay the welcome tour**. | | **First run** | A short conversation in the chat, not a form: what you are building, who feels the problem, the job they are trying to get done, then where it hurts. One question at a time, with a reflection before the next ask, quick replies, and **Explore on my own** always visible. Skipping is allowed; answers and progress are kept as a draft. Re-open it any time with `/start`, the home stage's context pill, or Settings. | | **Hero** | One rotating headline above the composer: a greeting (time of day, plus your name if you set one in Settings), the product/job you set up, what is already on the canvas, or an intent-first prompt such as *What are you trying to win this quarter?* It cycles every few seconds and stays still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. | | **Starter cards** | Below the headline, three canvas-aware conversation cards pair a clear next move with a short reason: **Sharpen an opportunity**, **Pressure-test a bet** or **Find the next opportunity**, and **Capture what you heard** or **Name the job**. Select one to start that prompt in the thread; the cards disappear once the conversation begins. **Opportunity landscape** remains a separate, quiet shortcut. | | **Composer** | Docked at the bottom of the transcript. `Enter` sends, `Shift`+`Enter` adds a line, `Cmd/Ctrl`+`K` focuses it, `/` opens the command palette, and the paperclip attaches a text file or an image. Files can also be dropped anywhere on the composer or pasted from the clipboard, and each one is shown with a size (and a thumbnail, for images) plus a remove control before it is sent; a file the studio cannot read is refused with the reason instead of becoming a chip that promises content the model will never see. The hint row's **Model** control lists the ids the configured backend reports and writes the choice through the same Settings store as the Base URL field. The send button becomes a stop button while a reply streams. | | **Bar** | The only persistent chrome: home, new conversation, catch-up, live model status, and settings. There is no navigation drawer to compete with the thread. | | **Rail** | Above the conversation, and only once the thread has produced something: `Landscape · N`, `Job map · N`, `Evidence · N`, `What I know · N`. Every item is derived from the canvas and the memory, so the strip is a record of the work rather than a fixed menu. | | **Lens** | A view docks to the right of the thread on wide screens and becomes a full-height sheet on narrow ones. The transcript and the composer stay on screen and stay usable; `Esc`, **Close**, or the rail chip closes it. Every lens ends in one sentence that re-enters the conversation — *Ask which to chase*, *Walk me through the job*, *Weigh the evidence* — so leaving a view is never a return to a menu. Settings and catch-up use the same lens. | Replies render Markdown (headings, lists, emphasis, inline and fenced code). While a turn has produced no text yet, an activity line names the phase (*Waking the model*, *Opening your studio tools*, *Thinking*) with a shimmer and an elapsed hint; the phase is announced once to assistive technology, and the reply is marked busy until it settles so a screen reader reads the answer, not every token. Reasoning sits above the answer in a disclosure that opens while it is being written and collapses to *Thought for Ns* afterwards, and every tool call is a trace chip with the source the turn actually read. ### Slash commands === website refs === website/templates/_cards.html:73:{% macro impact_simulation(data) %} website/templates/_cards.html:74:

def test_fetch_canvas_labels_a_partial_hydration(monkeypatch) -> None:
    _FakeClient.calls = []
    _FakeClient.error = None
    _FakeClient.payloads = {"get_jobs": json.dumps([{"id": "job-1"}])}
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
    monkeypatch.setattr(mcp_data, "McpClient", _FakeClient)

    raw = mcp_data.fetch_canvas

    async def _run() -> dict[str, Any]:
        # Only the jobs call succeeds; the per-job lookups fail, which the
        # client surfaces as warnings without losing the jobs it did read.
        original = _FakeClient.call_tool

        async def call_tool(self: _FakeClient, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
            if name in ("get_job_map", "get_outcomes", "list_evidence"):
                raise RuntimeError("read failed")
            return await original(self, name, arguments)

        _FakeClient.call_tool = call_tool  # type: ignore[method-assign]
        try:
            return await raw("http://mcp")
        finally:
            _FakeClient.call_tool = original  # type: ignore[method-assign]

    payload = asyncio.run(_run())

    assert payload["source"] == "mcp"
    assert payload["warnings"]
    assert payload["provenance"]["kind"] == "live"
    assert payload["provenance"]["reason"] == "partial_hydration"

        "record_counts": {
            "jobs": len(jobs),
            "steps": len(steps),

            "evidence": len(evidence),

    }

The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a
paragraph, the agent renders one **inline in the conversation**: a scored
outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a

- **The sidecar is catalog-agnostic.** The SPA sends the catalog with each turn;

doing the work.

artifact in the conversation, never to send the PM to a panel, and to end each

No surface may lie: label every demo, seed, and simulated signal
> **TL;DR** — The Studio shows you things it made up and never tells you so. Right now a first-time user sees three invented notifications ("Friction Collapse Simulation Complete"), a demo job called "JOB-402 / Sync Environment Secrets", and a Settings panel listing Gong, Slack and telemetry that can never connect — all presented as if they were real. After this issue, every piece of data in the Studio wears a label saying where it came from, demo data is visibly demo data, anything simulated is visibly simulated, and the two surfaces that pretend to be connected are either made real or removed. Nothing else about the product changes.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/studio` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | — |
| **Related PRs** | #63, #65, #66, #70 |
| **Blocks** | #79, #81, #95 |

---

## The problem

The Living Studio is a product where a person states intent and the system returns signals. That contract only works if every signal is real. Today it is not.

**1. Seed data is served as production data.** When the MCP server is unreachable or returns no jobs, `fetch_canvas` returns the demo seed:

- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/mcp_data.py:31` and `:82` — `seed_payload()` is returned when MCP is unreachable or empty.
- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/seed.py:1-101` — the seed is a fictional product, a fictional job (`JOB-402`, "Sync Environment Secrets Across Microservices"), fictional outcomes with fabricated importance/satisfaction numbers.
- The projection already carries the truth: the payload includes `"source": "seed"` and the SPA type declares it (`apps/studio/src/types.ts:27-32`). **Nothing in the UI ever reads it.**

**2. The "Catch Up" feed is fed by a demo button.** `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:402-433` — `simulateBackgroundEvent` picks one of three hardcoded strings at random and pushes it as a notification. It is wired to a button literally labelled **"+ Simulate update"** (`apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx:127-134`). There is no `/api/notifications` route, no server-side event source, no polling, no SSE subscription outside the chat request, and no connector path that produces a notification.

**3. A first-time user is shown fabricated activity as history.** `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:79-113` — `SEED_NOTIFICATIONS` contains three invented notifications, including "Friction Collapse Simulation Complete" and "New Customer Telemetry Signal". They are loaded whenever `localStorage` has no `studio.notifications` key (`:250-260`). The README tells the user to *"use the bell to catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away"* — which is exactly the fabrication.

**4. Settings lists three integrations that can never be connected.** `apps/studio/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:134-148` — "Gong transcripts", "Slack friction stream", and "Product telemetry" are static list items with a permanent `status-dot is-unknown`. They are not the real connector presets (`packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/catalog.py:236` lists 16 real presets), so a person reading Settings cannot tell which integrations are actually available.

**5. The docs describe the stub as shipped.** `docs/architecture/notifications.md:1-6` is titled *"Memory Recording for Notification/Alert System in Studio"* and lists what was "added". It never says the feed is seeded and simulated. `docs/living-studio.md:45,47` documents the catch-up bar button and lens as if a real signal system exists.

**6. The agent can render a card whose numbers are invented.** `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx:176-227` — the `impact-simulation` card takes `before[]`, `after[]`, `metrics[]`, and `verdict` entirely as `props`. There is no Bet/Simulation entity, no MCP tool, and no computation anywhere in the repository. Whatever the model writes is displayed as a measured before/after. The catalog even advertises it as *"a before/after simulation of a bet"* (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:198-203`).

**7. A non-existent feature is advertised on the public site.** `website/tools/sync-readme.py:254` renders a "Causal Lineage" mention into the site copy. There is no lineage model, tool, or graph in the repository.

## What a person experiences

A person opens the Studio for the first time. Instead of a wall of invented activity, they see the empty product, and a single honest line: *"No opportunities yet. Tell me the job your customers are trying to get done."* If the backend is unreachable, a persistent amber strip says **"Demo data — the ODI server is not reachable"** and every card carries a `DEMO` chip. If a person deliberately asks the agent to *simulate* an impact bet, the simulation card is rendered with a visible **"Simulated — no model behind this number"** ribbon, and the numbers are never presented as measurements. The Settings panel lists the sixteen connectors that actually exist and connects to them, and the three rows that never could connect are gone. Nothing in the Studio asserts something the system does not know.

## Specification

### 1.1 Provenance on the canvas projection

Extend the canvas payload with an explicit, machine-readable provenance object, and make the SPA render it.

**Backend** — `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/mcp_data.py`:

- `fetch_canvas` and `fetch_local_canvas` must both return a `provenance` object:

```python
{
    "kind": "live" | "seed" | "empty",
    "reason": str | None,        # e.g. "mcp_unreachable", "no_jobs", "local_store_empty"
    "generated_at": str,          # ISO-8601 UTC
    "record_counts": {"jobs": int, "steps": int, "outcomes": int, "evidence": int},
}
```

- `kind` is `"live"` only when the read came from the repository. It is `"seed"` only when `seed_payload()` was substituted, and `reason` must then be non-null. It is `"empty"` when the repository is genuinely empty — **this is a distinct, non-ugly state and must never be confused with an error**.

- Add `provenance: CanvasProvenance` to `CanvasData`.
- `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkbenchRail.tsx:26-60` — render a persistent `DEMO` / `OFFLINE` chip in the rail header whenever `provenance.kind !== "live"`. The chip is not dismissible while the condition holds.
- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx` — when `provenance.kind === "seed"`, render an inline banner above the matrix: *"Demo data. Nothing here comes from your research."* with a link to Settings → Connectors.

### 1.2 Seeded notifications must be labeled and separable

**Frontend** — `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:79-113`:

- Add `simulated: boolean` to the `StudioNotification` type (`apps/studio/src/types.ts:88-104`).
- `SEED_NOTIFICATIONS` entries are `simulated: true` and their `source` is `"demo"`.

- `apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx:197-204` — the empty state copy must say plainly that nothing has happened yet, and must not imply a backlog.

### 1.3 The simulator must be unmistakably a simulator

- `apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx:127-134` — the "+ Simulate update" button stays (it is a legitimate developer affordance) but every notification it creates renders a **"Simulated"** badge (`simulated === true`), and simulated notifications are visually distinct (a dashed border, a muted palette) and are excluded from the "While you were away" executive summary counters.

### 1.4 Settings must list what actually exists

- `apps/studio/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:134-148` — **delete** the three hardcoded rows ("Gong transcripts", "Slack friction stream", "Product telemetry").
- Replace them with a real list rendered from `GET /api/connectors/catalog` (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:95-97`), grouped by the five `CapabilityArea` values from `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/catalog.py:19-33`. Each row shows the preset id, its auth type (`token` / `oauth` / `none`), and a connect affordance that uses the existing `POST /api/connectors` route (`router.py:109-117`).
- If the catalog request fails, render an explicit error row — not an empty `<select>` (see #91).

### 1.5 The impact-simulation card must declare itself

- `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx:176-227` — the `impact-simulation` card must accept and require a `provenance` prop with one of `"simulated" | "measured"`. `"measured"` is only legal if a real computation backs it; until #95 lands there is no such computation, so **the only legal value today is `"simulated"`**.

A model that renders an impact simulation without declaring it simulated is rejected and asked to fix it, exactly like the existing `render_ui` validation-failure path (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:332-340`).

- `docs/architecture/notifications.md` — rewrite. It must state, in one sentence, that the catch-up feed's content is currently produced by a local simulator, and point at the issue that replaces it.
- `docs/living-studio.md:45,47` — add the same caveat to the catch-up description.
